title: Bases of flat modules over a local ring with nilpotent maximal ideal
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a local ring whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is nilpotent ($\mathfrak m^N=0$ for some $N$; e.g. an Artinian local ring), and let $M$ be a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], not necessarily finitely generated. Let $A$ be a set and $(x_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}$ a family of elements of $M$, with images $\overline x_\alpha\in M/\mathfrak mM$. Then the following are equivalent: (1) $(\overline x_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}$ is a basis of the $R/\mathfrak m$-vector space $M/\mathfrak mM$; (2) $(x_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}$ is a basis of $M$ as an $R$-module (the $R$-linear map $\bigoplus_{\alpha\in A}R\to M$, $e_\alpha\mapsto x_\alpha$, is an isomorphism).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 051F (lemma-local-artinian-basis-when-flat, line 24295); its proof uses Nakayama's Lemma Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK, nilpotent case) and Lemma Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero, line 9037)

proof.text: Set I = maximalIdeal R and Q = I times M. Mathlib TensorProduct.quotTensorEquivQuotSMul M I gives (R/I) tensor M isomorphic to M/Q [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring]. Upgrade this R-linear equivalence to an R/I-linear equivalence by LinearEquiv.extendScalarsOfSurjective and surjectivity of the quotient ring map. If b is an R-basis with b(a)=x(a), its scalar extension Basis.baseChange (R/I), transported along this equivalence, is the quotient basis with value the class of x(a).

Conversely, suppose b is a basis of M/Q consisting of the classes of x(a). Transport b backwards through the preceding equivalence. Its family is a -> 1 tensor x(a), so it is linearly independent over R/I. Mathlib Module.IsLocalRing.linearIndependent_of_flat applies to the arbitrary flat module M [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and this family to give LinearIndependent R x. This replaces the planned kernel and tensor-exact-sequence argument; the Mathlib theorem requires neither finite generation nor finite presentation.

Let L = span_R(range x). The quotient basis spans M/Q over R/I. Mathlib Submodule.restrictScalars_span, using surjectivity R -> R/I, shows the same family spans over R. Submodule.map_span identifies this span with the image of L under the quotient map. Thus Q.mkQ composed with L.subtype is surjective. For any quotient element choose a lift z in L; the class of z in L/IL maps to that element. Hence the induced map L/IL -> M/IM is surjective. A zero power I^k supplies a positive zero power I^(k+1). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-nilpotent] to L.subtype: L -> M to conclude the inclusion is surjective, hence L = top.

Apply Mathlib Basis.mk to the linear independence from step 2 and the spanning equality from step 3. Basis.mk_apply proves that the constructed basis takes value x(a) at every a. Together with step 1 this proves the equivalence for the original arbitrary index type and module universes.
